text: This is Tally. A running tally of the outside world.

If you invest at pre-seed, your edge is noticing early: who is hiring, who shipped, who just raised, how big the new YC batch is. Today that lives in tabs, newsletters and a spreadsheet. Alert tools watch one page for one user, and they can't count or add things up.

Tally turns those questions into live numbers. This is an investor's board: the size of the current YC batch, funding announced by AI agent startups this month, and hiring and launches at the companies I'm watching. Each tile shows the value, the change, and when it was last checked.

To add a company, I type its name. Linear is already in the shared catalog, so a pack of six numbers arrives at once: funding, open roles, launches, price, rating and stars. Someone else asked first, and I reuse their work.
Every number shows how it is made. I open Gamma's open engineering roles: the source, the recipe, a ledger of entries, each stored once by its link, and the Telem calls behind it.
Now I press Check now. Telem Search runs with Tavily pinned, Telem Fetch reads the job board, and the count goes from twelve to thirteen. The new role is highlighted, with its link.
The change log shows only what moved, including changes that Telem monitors found on their own, without anyone pressing a button.
And the Telem trace shows the engine: every call, the providers that answered, latency, estimated cost, and the calls saved by sharing.
That sharing is the business. One refresh serves everyone who follows a number, so the cost per user falls as the catalog grows. And history cannot be bought later.
The recipes are open source. The product is the hosted runtime: free to read, nineteen dollars a month for everything live. It is running today, with sign-in and billing.
Tally. Ask for a number, keep it current. We are looking for angels and pre-seed funds as design partners. Thank you.
